processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The steel was fabricated using the high-frequency vacuum induction melting furnace.
Hot-forged into billets with a thickness of 110 mm at 1150 °C then air cooling to room temperature. Prior step common to all hot-rolled samples.
The hot-forged billets were initially reheated at 1150 °C before hot rolling.
Hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 35 mm (hot-rolling reduction: 68%), denoted HR68. Number of passes during hot rolling was 6 for HR68.
After hot rolling the samples were water quenched to room temperature; this fast cooling produced the κ-carbides by spinodal decomposition and ordering.

defect_interactions.interaction_type: strain/stress concentration at (Nb,Mo,W)C–austenite interfaces leading to microcrack nucleation and microvoid formation
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: The (Nb,Mo,W)C particles located at the austenite grain boundaries act as hard second-phase particles leading to strain/stress concentration at their interfaces due to deformation discrepancy with the austenite matrix, tending to serve as preferential nucleation sites for microcracks; the concentration could be partially alleviated through debonding of intragranular (Nb,Mo,W)C particles and subsequent formation of microvoids.

interfaces.interface_notes: For HR68 the submicron-sized particle was identified as a Nb-rich, Fe/Mn/Al-depleted (Nb,Mo,W)C particle with FCC structure (SAED [110] zone axis); no particle outline for C, Mo or W in EDS maps.

phase_interfaces.coherence: incoherent (bypassed by dislocations through the Orowan mechanism)
coherent and shearable (shearing generates anti-phase boundaries)

interfaces.slip_behavior: Predominant dislocation planar glide producing planar slip bands and Taylor lattice; slip bands refine with strain and then microbands with ill-defined and distinct boundaries form. For HR68, microbands were already observed at engineering strain 0.2.

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: Effective grain size including annealing twin boundaries: 11.55 μm for HR68; Σ3 twin boundary fraction 60% (by length relative to total boundary length with misorientation >15°).

phases_present.grain_size: 27.02 μm (excluding annealing twin boundaries); 11.55 μm effective grain size (including twins)
phases_present.morphology: equiaxed grains with first-order annealing twins (Σ3 60°<111>)
micron-sized polygonal particles along rolling direction at grain boundaries and grain interior (1–25 μm); submicron-sized spherical particles homogeneously distributed in austenite matrix
nano-sized particles homogeneously precipitated inside austenite grains (formed by spinodal decomposition and ordering during water quenching)

precipitates.distribution: homogeneously distributed in the austenite matrix (also along grain boundaries)
along the rolling direction at grain boundaries and grain interior (stringers)

precipitates.coherency: coherent/sharable (sheared by moving dislocations; produce APBs)
precipitates.distribution: homogeneously precipitated inside the austenite grains during water quenching

structures.overall_structure: Fully austenitic (FCC) hot-rolled microstructure consisting of equiaxed FCC austenite grains with a large fraction of first-order annealing twins (Σ3 60°<111> grain boundaries); two populations of second-phase particles and nano-sized κ-carbides present.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Uniaxial tensile tests on an MTS tensile machine; extensometer used; interrupted at engineering strains of 10%, 20%, 40% before fracture.
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: standard tensile samples cut along the rolling direction (RD), gauge length 25 mm, diameter 5 mm

strain_hardening_rate: Strain-hardening rate maintained at a high level of ~2000 MPa over a wide range of plastic strain (three-staged strain-hardening behaviour; stage II increase due to slip-band refinement)
tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress–strain curve of HR68 (red curve) in Fig. 5a; peaks between the 900 and 1000 MPa gridlines near ε ≈ 0.45 and ends near ε ≈ 0.57.
